mainTopic: Does 'since he could' (הואיל) work for an עירוב? The גמרא discusses bringing the עירוב to its place, an עירוב in a cupboard that could be tilted, and an עירוב placed in a deep pit.
overview: On the previous amud, רבי ירמיה argued 'since he could' (הואיל): since a person could tilt a basket, it counts as if he did. The גמרא asks why that logic does not mean a person need not actually bring his עירוב to its place. רבי זירא answers that requiring him to bring it is a גזירה because of a יום טוב that falls right after שבת, when the עירוב truly cannot be carried there. Next, a ברייתא rules that an עירוב in a cupboard (מגדל) below ten טפחים is invalid for someone resting on top of it. The גמרא asks why he cannot simply tilt the cupboard so that its top comes down within ten. רבי ירמיה answers that the cupboard is nailed down. רבא answers that it is a very tall cupboard, so even a slight tilt would push its top beyond four אמות. When asked why he does not just use a window and a rope, the גמרא says the case has neither. Finally, the גמרא turns to the משנה's case of an עירוב in a deep pit and begins asking where the pit is located, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not say it counts as if he brought the עירוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that the עירוב must actually be brought to its place. Using the 'since he could' logic, simply being able to bring it should be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why must he actually bring it? Let us say: since he could have brought it if he wanted to, then even though he did not bring it, it should count as if he did!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the 'since he could' idea that רבי ירמיה just used and asks why it does not work here. Here the rule is that a person must actually bring his עירוב to its spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה said that something a person is able to do can count as if he did it. If so, the fact that he could carry the עירוב to the place should be enough. But the halacha requires him to really bring it, so the principle seems to fail here. That puts רבי ירמיה's logic in question.

phrases.english: Why?
phrases.notes: Why does the source require that the עירוב actually be brought?

phrases.english: Let us say: since if he wished to bring it
he could bring it,
even though he did not bring it
it should be considered as if he brought it!
phrases.notes: This is the same 'since he could' logic as רבי ירמיה's basket case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? נֵימָא: כֵּיוָן דְּאִי בָּעֵי אַמְטוֹיֵי מָצֵי מַמְטֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues earlier. It challenges רבי ירמיה's 'since he could tilt it' reasoning by pointing to a case where ability alone is not enough.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'since he could' (הואיל) principle used by רבי ירמיה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If being able to do something counts as doing it, then being able to bring the עירוב should count as bringing it. Yet the halacha requires actually bringing it.

steps.title: A גזירה because of יום טוב right after שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that requiring the עירוב to be actually brought is a rabbinic decree. It was made because of a יום טוב that falls after שבת, when the 'he could bring it' logic does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: It is a decree because of a יום טוב that falls right after שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the challenge. He says the strict rule is a rabbinic safeguard, not a rejection of the 'since he could' idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When יום טוב comes right after שבת, the עירוב for יום טוב cannot be carried to its spot on שבת. So in that case it truly could not be brought, and 'since he could' does not apply. To keep people from mixing up the cases, the חכמים required actually bringing the עירוב every time.

keyTerms.meaning: a rabbinic decree made as a protective fence

keyTerms.term: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר שַׁבָּת
keyTerms.meaning: a Festival that falls right after Shabbat

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the 'since he could' principle still stands. The rule requiring the עירוב to actually be brought is a rabbinic safeguard, not proof that the principle is wrong.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
It is a decree on account of a Festival
that falls after Shabbat.
phrases.notes: On שבת he cannot carry the עירוב there, so in that case he truly could not bring it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: גְּזֵירָה מִשּׁוּם יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר שַׁבָּת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic decree (גזירה): the strict rule is a safeguard, not a denial of the principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The requirement to bring the עירוב shows that 'since he could' does not work at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Strictly, 'since he could' would work. The חכמים still required actually bringing it because of יום טוב after שבת.

steps.title: A ברייתא about an עירוב in a wall or a cupboard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about where an עירוב may be placed. Whether it is valid depends on whether it is above or below ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected: Suppose a person intended to rest in the public domain and placed his עירוב in a wall. If it is below ten טפחים, his עירוב is valid. If it is above ten טפחים, his עירוב is not valid. Suppose he intended to rest on top of a dovecote or on top of a cupboard. If the עירוב is above ten טפחים, it is valid. If it is below ten טפחים, it is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא as material for another objection. This step sets up the challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב works only if the person and his עירוב are in domains where he could carry it to himself. In a wall, above ten טפחים is a private domain while he is in the public domain, so it fails. On top of a cupboard he is in a private domain, so an עירוב placed below ten טפחים (a כרמלית) fails.

keyTerms.meaning: ten handbreadths, the height that changes the domain
here: a large cupboard or closet (not a tower)

steps.confusionAlert: Here מִגְדָּל means a large cupboard, not a tower. That is why the next step can talk about tilting it.

phrases.english: He raised an objection against him:
If one intended to rest in the public domain,
and placed his eiruv in a wall,
below ten handbreadths, his eiruv is valid;

phrases.aramaic: לְמַעְלָה מֵעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים — אֵין עֵירוּבוֹ עֵירוּב.
phrases.english: above ten handbreadths, his eiruv is not valid.
phrases.notes: The עירוב is in a רשות היחיד while he is in the רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: If one intended to rest on top of a dovecote
or on top of a cupboard,
above ten handbreadths, his eiruv is valid.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַטָּה מֵעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים — אֵין עֵירוּבוֹ עֵירוּב.
phrases.english: below ten handbreadths, his eiruv is not valid.
phrases.notes: Below ten is a כרמלית, so he cannot bring the עירוב up to himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי זירא's answer, a new source is brought to test the 'since he could' principle again.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'since he could' (הואיל) principle of רבי ירמיה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: the ברייתא invalidates an עירוב below ten טפחים in a cupboard. The next step will argue that the cupboard could have been tilted.

steps.title: Why not say he could tilt the cupboard?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא rules the עירוב invalid. He could tilt the cupboard and bring its top, where he plans to rest, down to within ten טפחים, the same domain as the עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is that? Here too let us say: since he could tilt it and bring it within ten טפחים, it should be valid!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the actual challenge comes. The גמרא applies the 'since he could tilt it' idea to the cupboard in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'since he could' works, the cupboard case should be valid. He could tilt the cupboard so that its top, where he means to rest, comes down to within ten טפחים. Then he and his עירוב would be in the same domain. Since the ברייתא says it is not valid, the principle seems to be contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: since he is able (the 'since he could' principle)

phrases.english: But why? Here too let us say:
since he can tilt it
and bring it within ten handbreadths!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? הָכִי נָמֵי נֵימָא: הוֹאִיל וְיָכוֹל לִנְטוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the objection that Step 3 set up.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in the ברייתא that the עירוב below ten טפחים is not valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the 'since he could tilt it' logic, the עירוב should be valid. The ברייתא rejects it, which contradicts רבי ירמיה.

steps.title: The cupboard is nailed down
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers that the ברייתא is talking about a cupboard nailed in place, which cannot be tilted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Here we are dealing with a cupboard that is nailed down.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה defends his principle. He limits the ברייתא to a special case where tilting is impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'since he could' principle works only when the action is really possible. A nailed cupboard cannot be tilted, so the principle does not apply, and the ברייתא's ruling fits. The principle stays intact.

keyTerms.meaning: here we are dealing with... (limits the case)

steps.whatToRemember: The 'since he could' principle survives both challenges. Requiring the עירוב to be brought is a גזירה because of יום טוב after שבת. According to רבי ירמיה, the cupboard case involves a nailed cupboard that cannot be tilted. רבא gives a different explanation in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
Here we are dealing with a cupboard that is nailed down.
phrases.notes: Since it is fastened, it cannot be tilted, so 'since he could' does not apply.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: הָכָא בְּמִגְדָּל מְסוּמָּר עָסְקִינַן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about any cupboard, even one that can be tilted, which would disprove 'since he could'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a nailed cupboard that cannot be tilted, so the principle is not contradicted.

steps.title: רבא: The cupboard is very tall, so tilting it moves its top beyond four אמות
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer to the question of why the person cannot just tilt the cupboard. The cupboard is so tall that, if tilted, its top (where he intends to rest) would end up outside the four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can even say the ברייתא is talking about a cupboard that is not nailed down. But here we are dealing with a tall cupboard. If he tilted it a little, its top would go outside the four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the same question that רבי ירמיה answered, but in a different way. The cupboard can move, but it is so tall that tilting it would make its top land outside the four אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in Step 4 was: why not tilt the cupboard and bring its top down to within ten טפחים? רבי ירמיה said the cupboard is nailed down, so it cannot be tilted. רבא says it can be tilted, but because it is so tall, even a slight tilt would move its top, the spot where he intends to rest, beyond the four אמות. So tilting does not help.

keyTerms.meaning: Four cubits, the small area that counts as a person's spot

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not disagreeing with the ruling of the ברייתא. Both he and רבי ירמיה agree the עירוב is invalid. They only disagree about why tilting the cupboard does not help.

phrases.english: Rava said:
You can even say it is a cupboard that is not nailed down,
phrases.notes: This rejects the need for רבי ירמיה's 'nailed' answer.

phrases.english: and here we are dealing with a tall cupboard,
so that if he tilts it a little,
it goes outside the four cubits.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the top of the cupboard, where he means to rest, not the עירוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question in Step 4, instead of רבי ירמיה's answer in Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (a tall cupboard instead of a nailed one)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think a loose cupboard can always be tilted to bring the עירוב within reach.
steps.terutzMaskana: A tall cupboard cannot be tilted without moving its top, his intended resting spot, beyond the four אמות, so tilting does not help and the עירוב is invalid.

steps.title: Why not pull the עירוב out with a rope through a window?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's case. If the cupboard has a window and the person has a rope, he could get the עירוב out without tilting anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: What exactly is the case? If there is a window and a rope, let him bring the עירוב out using the window and the rope!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's case. If there is a window in the cupboard and a rope available, he can get the עירוב without tilting the cupboard at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer assumed the only way to reach the עירוב is to tilt the cupboard. The גמרא points out another way: lower a rope through a window and pull the עירוב out. If that is possible, the עירוב is reachable and should be valid.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What exactly are we talking about?

phrases.english: What is the case?
If there is a window and a rope,
let him bring it with the window and rope!
phrases.notes: Lower the rope through the window and pull the עירוב out.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דְּאִיכָּא כַּוְּותָא וּמִתְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's tall-cupboard case from Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the עירוב cannot be reached in a tall, loose cupboard
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There may be another way to reach the עירוב (a window and a rope), so tilting would not be necessary and the עירוב should be valid.

steps.title: There is no window and no rope
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is one where the cupboard has no window and the person has no rope.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where he does not have a window and a rope.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case: there is no window and no rope, so tilting is the only option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no window and no rope, the only way to reach the עירוב would be tilting the cupboard. Tilting would carry the top of the cupboard, where he intends to rest, outside the four אמות, so רבא's explanation stands and the עירוב is invalid.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's invalid cupboard case is explained in two ways: רבי ירמיה says the cupboard is nailed down, and רבא says it is a tall cupboard with no window and no rope. In both, there is no way to bring the עירוב within reach.

phrases.english: Where he does not have a window and a rope.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: A window and rope might be available to pull the עירוב out.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case has no window and no rope, so the עירוב truly cannot be reached.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: an עירוב placed in a deep pit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to a new line of the משנה: an עירוב placed in a pit, even one a hundred אמות deep, is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If he placed the עירוב in a pit, even one a hundred אמות deep, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new topic. It quotes the משנה's case of an עירוב placed in a deep pit, setting up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about an עירוב placed high up. Now the גמרא looks at the opposite case, an עירוב placed deep down in a pit, which the משנה says is valid. This quote prepares the next step, where the גמרא asks where this pit is located.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc., and so on (the quote continues in the משנה)

phrases.english: If he placed it in a pit,
even a hundred cubits deep, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה rules this עירוב valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְתָנוֹ בְּבוֹר אֲפִילּוּ עָמוֹק מֵאָה אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the cupboard discussion and opens analysis of a new clause in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב placed in a pit, even a very deep one, is valid.

steps.title: Where is this pit located?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the pit is located and starts with the first possibility: a רשות היחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: This pit, where is it located? If you say it is located in a רשות היחיד...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which domain the pit is in. It begins testing the first option, a רשות היחיד, and the discussion continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The location of the pit matters because the rules of carrying on שבת depend on the domain. Whether the person could bring the עירוב up depends on where the pit is and where the person stands. The גמרא opens with 'If you say' (אילימא), which signals that it will test this option and probably reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces an option that will be tested)
A private domain, an enclosed area where carrying is allowed on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is cut off in the middle. The גמרא has not answered yet, and the 'רשות היחיד' option is only the first one being tested.

phrases.english: This pit, where is it located?
If you say it is located in a private domain,
phrases.notes: The thought continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a clarifying question about the משנה clause quoted in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In which domain the pit containing the עירוב is located
